title: Observability-First SDK Onramp: Canary Integration & Error Mitigation Playbook
author: Maya Chen
summary: Opinionated, production-ready onboarding playbook for teams integrating Redwood SDKs that prioritizes observability, canonical error mitigation, and safe canary rollouts.
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook describes an observability-first SDK onramp for Redwood customers and internal teams adopting our client libraries. It standardizes tracing, metrics, and logs, and ties them to a safe canary procedure and a compact set of canonical fixes for the top 8 support patterns we see in the field.

Who should use this: SDK integrators, platform engineers, SREs, and developer-experience engineers responsible for shipping LLM features with Redwood.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-detect: surface failures within 90s of incidence.
- Reduce time-to-recover: provide clear mitigations and runbook links so developers can resolve 80% of common issues without escalation.
- Safe rollouts: enable canary releases that detect regressions in latency, token cost, and quality.

Prerequisites
1) Team has a Redwood API key and a dedicated test model route (e.g., model: redwood/xxl:2025-04-canary).
2) CI that can run integration smoke tests and a lightweight synthetic quality test.
3) A monitoring workspace (Grafana/Datadog) with ability to ingest metrics and traces.

High-level workflow
1. Integrate SDK basics and add observability hooks (tracing, metrics, structured logs).
2. Run a local smoke suite (latency, auth, basic generation) as part of CI.
3. Deploy canary (1–5% traffic) with enhanced sampling and compare metrics against baseline.
4. Automatically rollback or escalate based on SLO breach or quality regression.

Step-by-step integration guide
1) SDK Initialization (example, Node.js):

```js
// ./src/redwoodClient.js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  telemetry: { enabled: true, sampleRate: 0.5 }, // default 50% for canary
  retries: { maxAttempts: 2, backoffMs: 200 }
});
module.exports = client;
```

Notes: enable telemetry during canary (sampleRate >= 0.5) for richer tracing. For heavy production, keep sampleRate <= 0.1.

2) Tracing (OpenTelemetry example, Python):

```py
from opentelemetry import trace
from redwood_otlp_exporter import RedwoodOTLPExporter  # internal adapter
tracer_provider = TracerProvider()
tracer_provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(RedwoodOTLPExporter()))
trace.set_tracer_provider(tracer_provider)
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)

with tracer.start_as_current_span('redwood.request') as span:
    span.set_attribute('redwood.model', 'redwood/xxl')
    span.set_attribute('redwood.route', '/v1/chat')
    # call client here
```

3) Metrics to emit (recommended):
- redwood.requests.total (counter) – labels: route, model, env, region
- redwood.requests.success (counter) – labels: route, model, status_code_class
- redwood.latency.p50/p90/p99 (histogram) – labels: route, model, env
- redwood.kvcache.hits (counter) and redwood.kvcache.misses (counter) – for private deployments
- redwood.tokens.generated (counter) – monthly billing reconciliation

Configuration reference table
| key | recommended default | notes |
|-----|--------------------:|-------|
| telemetry.sampleRate | "0.1" | 0.1 for prod, 0.5 for canaries and debug sessions |
| telemetry.endpoint | "https://otel-collector.redwood.internal:4317" | OTLP receiver for traces and metrics |
| retries.maxAttempts | "2" | Exponential backoff used; avoid retries for streaming endpoints |
| batch.maxTokens | "4096" | Max aggregation window for batching; tune by workload |

Canonical error patterns and fixes (top patterns observed)
1. AUTH_EXPIRED / 401 on long-running jobs
   - Symptom: Requests failing after ~30m even though token was valid at start.
   - Cause: Token rotation missing in long-lived workers.
   - Fix: Use short-lived job tokens and refresh before each job chunk. Add span attribute redwood.token_expires_at to traces.

2. TIMEOUT (client-side)
   - Symptom: Frequent 504 in client logs, server shows healthy 2xx responses.
   - Cause: Client HTTP timeout < server tail-latency for larger sequences.
   - Fix: Increase client request timeout to 45s and enable streaming response handling. Update SDK config: timeouts.requestMs = 45000.

3. HIGH_P50_CANARY_REGRESSION
   - Symptom: Canary shows p50 +30% relative to baseline, p90 unchanged.
   - Cause: Misconfigured batching window or different model variant with slower kernels.
   - Fix: Check batch.maxTokens and kernel profile. Re-run micro-benchmarks. If confirmed, roll back canary and open an infra perf investigation.

4. OUTPUT_QUALITY_DRIFT
   - Symptom: Eval prompt sets show lower BLEU/ROUGE/qualitative score on canary.
   - Fix: Abort canary, capture prompt set, run model-vs-model regression in eval harness, and tag candidate for model-onboarding team.

5. KVCACHE_STALLS
   - Symptom: Increased latency for multi-turn chat; kvcache misses spike.
   - Cause: Cache key mismatch due to route or role normalization.
   - Fix: Normalize conversation IDs and enable server-side prefix caching. Add labels to cache metrics for route and session_id.

6. RATE_LIMIT_BURSTS (429)
   - Symptom: Spikes of 429 during rollout or test storms.
   - Fix: Implement client-side leaky-bucket with jitter and exponential backoff. Define a descending retry policy for 429 vs 5xx.

7. BILLING_RECONCILE_MISMATCH
   - Symptom: Monthly tokens.generated totals differ between client accounting and billing.
   - Fix: Emit redwood.tokens.generated with consistent tokenization settings and record model_version label. Compare with route-level billing exports.

8. OBSERVABILITY_BLACKHOLE
   - Symptom: No traces for a subset of requests in canary.
   - Cause: Telemetry endpoint misconfiguration or TLS issue.
   - Fix: Fallback to pushing traces to a debug bucket and re-enable with correct OTLP endpoint. Use SDK health probe: /_internal/telemetry/health.

Canary rollout checklist (recommended SLOs and gates)
- Baseline collection: 72h of production traffic or synthetic baseline for new routes.
- Traffic split: Start at 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over multiple hours/days depending on risk.
- Observability gates (must pass to advance):
  1) Latency: p50 increase <= 10% and p90 increase <= 5% over baseline.
  2) Error rate: total non-2xx <= 0.1% and 5xx <= 0.02%.
  3) Token unit cost: per-request tokens cost delta <= 3%.
  4) Quality: synthetic eval score delta <= 2 points on team-defined metric.
  5) KV cache hit rate: no >10% drop for multi-turn routes.

Automated rollback triggers (examples)
- Any single 5xx spike that increases 5xx rate >0.05% absolute AND is sustained >10 minutes.
- Latency p50 increase >20% for >15 minutes.
- Quality regression tripping the eval harness with p < 0.01 false positive tolerance.

Escalation and ownership
- First responder: owning feature team (contact in Slack #team-<feature> and PagerDuty).
- Second-line: Platform SRE (pager: SRE-Platform).
- Model-onboarding: notify Applied ML & Evals (label: model-onboard).
- For billing discrepancies: Finance + Billing Eng run reconciliation job using redwood.tokens.generated export.

Runbook snippets (quick commands)
- Canary snapshot compare (CLI):
```bash
redwoodctl canary diff --baseline=stable-2025-09-01 --candidate=canary-2025-11-01 --metrics latency,errors,tokens --out=canary-report.json
```
- Force rollback:
```bash
redwoodctl rollout abort --route /v1/chat --reason "canary-latency-regression"
```
- Telemetry health check (curl):
```bash
curl -sSf -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.internal/_internal/telemetry/health | jq .
```

Appendix: Example synthetic evaluation snippet (Python)
```py
from redwood_eval import EvalHarness
h = EvalHarness(route='/v1/chat', model='redwood/xxl:2025-04-canary')
prompts = ["Summarize: The company announced a new widget.", "Fix the grammar: I has a error."]
results = h.run(prompts, metrics=['perplexity','bleu','human_sim'])
print(results.summary())
```

Maintenance & updates
- This playbook should be reviewed quarterly or after any major SDK release. Add review notes in the page history and increment the version tag in the labels.

Ownership
- Playbook owner: Developer Experience (Maya Chen)
- Escalation: Platform SRE oncall

If you implement this playbook and hit a pattern that isn't covered, file an issue under the devx repo: https://git.redwood.internal/devx/observability-playbook/issues.
